alignments.note: Quantifying construct `כֹּל` takes its own word only; the chain's relational *of* belongs to the rectum under rule 19.
No article morpheme stands on the construct, so the *the* before *brethren* is supplied and joins this noun under rules 29 and 15.
Rectum of the chain takes the relational *of* (rule 19); anarthrous substantival participle takes the supplied *the* under rule 46, headed on the lexeme-bearing *poor* under rule 31.
Finite verb with its emphatic auxiliary *do*, headed on the lexical verb under rules 17 and 24.
Object suffix realized by *him* under rule 18.

`אַף כִּי` is rendered by the single fixed English expression *How much more*, of which no morpheme owns a part, so the two share one unit under rule 30 read as one rendering rather than one token. Neither morpheme carries content the other lacks, so the source head is the governing first morpheme under rule 23; the target head is the content word the phrase turns on by rule 31's subtraction, since dropping *more* leaves the comparison unstated. The competing reading would split *How much* from *more*, but neither piece is independently ownable.
Construct noun takes only its own English word.
Possessive suffix realized by *his* under rule 18.

Discontinuous under rule 25: the fronted question auxiliary *do* belongs to this verb, since no interrogative particle stands in the clause (rule 17's first limit). *go far* is a light verb plus complement, headed on *far*, which carries `רָחַק`'s lexeme, under rule 44.
Preposition takes the *from* written for it.
Suffix on the preposition realized by *him* under rule 18.
Predicative participle with the English subject pronoun realizing its person and number under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.

Supplied object pronoun (ASV italic, corroborating but not deciding, by rule 7). No object morpheme stands in the clause, so it answers to nothing and is `added` under rule 44; it is not folded into the participle merely because it stands inside its rendering. It is a separate run from the supplied *with*, which stands before a written noun.

Bare nominal with no preposition or object marker on it; the supplied instrumental *with* states what the noun contributes to its clause and belongs to it under rule 33, headed on the lexeme-bearing *words*. Rule 44 does not reach it, since the English verb's own object is the supplied *them*, not this noun.

No conjunction morpheme stands in this colon, so the coordinating *but* answers to nothing and is `added` under rule 14's closing sentences. It is not the negative's: rule 14 gives a negative a *nor* or *neither*, and `לֹא` already holds the rendering below.
Independent pronoun takes its own *they*; the clause's copula goes to the predicate under rule 20.

The negative is the predicate of the verbless clause `לֹא־הֵמָּה`, so the construction-supplied copula joins it under rule 20 and it heads on *gone*, which is what carries the negation here — dropping *gone* leaves *they are* saying nothing of the `לֹא`. The competing reading would mark `לֹא` `unrepresented` and call *are gone* a supplied lexical verb, but that would leave a written morpheme with no rendering while plain English answering to it stood unaligned.

review_notes: Variant WLC.PRO.19.7.v001 selected -> r01, compatible and covering s015; the unit carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 53 does not apply and `לֹא` is aligned as ordinary source text.

The marginal note *Or, He pursueth after words, which are nought* was read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text governs, so *with words* is aligned as printed and no relative clause is posited.

Two supplied runs are kept separate under rule 2: the italic *them* is a supplied object with no source morpheme, while the italic *with* stands before the written `אֲמָרִים` and is that noun's under rule 33.
